body.x: Voice commands could let an aircraft technician pull up a procedure or a torque value while both hands stay on the work, but two conditions get in the way. Hangar noise from running engines and power tools reaches 94 to 111 dB, and aviation and defense sites often operate closed networks with security requirements that rule out cloud-based speech services.
What if the entire voice pipeline, from speech recognition to document search, ran on the device itself?

Artaud AI Inc., a Seoul-based on-device voice AI company founded in April 2024 and led by CEO Jungho Kim, has built its products around that approach. It develops voice-conversational agents for aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), defense and industrial equipment maintenance, and it is a winner of the KES 2026 Innovation Awards. Headquartered in Gwanak-gu, the company takes part in Seoul National University's RISE program (Gwanak S Valley).

Artaud AI's pipeline combines speech recognition (ASR), context-based transcript correction and large language model (LLM)-based document retrieval (RAG). All three run on the device with no server or cloud connection, so the system can meet the security requirements of closed defense and aviation networks.

In environments of 94 to 111 dB, comparable to running aircraft engines and power tools, multi-speaker recognition picks out only the designated technician's speech. Terminology models are built from text data such as maintenance manuals, without collecting voice recordings. The company holds 2 registered Korean patents, 5 pending Korean applications and 1 international application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).

At KES 2026, Artaud AI is showing its On-Device Voice-Conversational Aircraft Maintenance Agent. Technicians can check aircraft status, report defects, follow maintenance procedures and record completed work by voice. Results appear as text on a tablet or laptop-class device, with links to the relevant manual sections.

The agent adds voice search and control on top of existing electronic manuals and work orders instead of replacing them, which the company says keeps deployment time and cost low. During the show, Artaud AI plans to demonstrate the agent using maintenance scenarios. It aims to win new domestic customers among airline maintenance divisions, MRO companies and defense contractors.

Artaud AI's domestic results center on aviation and defense. The company ran a voice-control pilot for Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETM) at Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) and is now developing the system for production use. It also holds a contract with KAI for IETM voice-control maintenance development, running from April 2026 to December 2028, and carried out a voice-control pilot for an MR-based computer-based training (CBT) system with IT Science.

Korean Air is the end user in a Ministry of SMEs and Startups public-private joint technology commercialization R&D program (procurement-linked type), under which Artaud AI is developing a maintenance agent linked to digital manuals from September 2026 to August 2028. A Ministry of SMEs and Startups global collaboration program with Intel is supporting optimization for Intel AI PCs. Under Incheon International Airport Corporation's 2026 Win-Win Startup and Venture Support Program, the company is running a voice search and control trial for technical manuals used in freighter conversion (P2F) at the airport's Aviation Complex from October to December 2026.

In the fourth quarter, Artaud AI also plans to verify a character error rate (CER) within 10% in hangar noise through an accredited test, then propose a pilot project based on the trial results and move to a license contract. The company has no exports yet. Through Incheon International Airport Corporation's global program, Global Tech On-France & Finland Slush, it aims to meet at least 3 potential European partners in France and Finland in November 2026, and to run a proof-of-concept (PoC) trial with one European partner in 2027 and sign a license contract in 2028. Artaud AI says European MRO companies already hold manuals based on the S1000D and ATA standards, so adding a voice layer without changing those manuals is easy to adopt.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Hosted by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and the Korea Electronics Association (KEA), the show expects 500 exhibitors, 1,100 booths and 70,000 visitors across six sectors. It opens from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Oct. 13 to Oct. 15 and from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Oct. 16, and the KES Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on the opening day.
